# **PURPOSE:**

When exploring our data, we noticed a few outliers and wanted to investigate the how much of an effect they had on our results. With a small sample size, as we have in this experiment, it is difficult to tell if they are true outliers or within a range of natural variation. Additionally, since all identified outliers are females, it is possible that reproductive status (a factor we did not control for, although all females tested were not visibly pregnant) is altering the thermal tolerance. Therefore, these analyses are for exploratory purposes only, and we will not be removing these outliers from our final reported data set. 

The analysis below is a repeat of the analyses found in *Final_temperature-analysis.Rmd* within the **Thermal Tolerance Analysis** folder. To run this current file, the *Temp ID - Completed Data.csv* from the **Thermal Tolerance Analysis** folder is required.

## Identifying outliers

```{r}

#calculate outliers for both CTmax and CTmin by species
df_flagged <- O.rawTempData %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  mutate(
    q1_max = quantile(CTmax.C, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3_max = quantile(CTmax.C, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_max = q3_max - q1_max,
    q1_min = quantile(CTmin.C, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3_min = quantile(CTmin.C, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_min = q3_min - q1_min,
    is_outlier_max = CTmax.C < (q1_max - 1.5 * iqr_max) | CTmax.C > (q3_max + 1.5 * iqr_max),
    is_outlier_min = CTmin.C < (q1_min - 1.5 * iqr_min) | CTmin.C > (q3_min + 1.5 * iqr_min)) %>%
  ungroup()

#visualize CTmin outliers
out.min <- ggplot(df_flagged, aes(x = CTmin.C, fill = is_outlier_min)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#d95f02"),
                    name = "Data Status",
                    labels = c("Normal", "Outlier"),
                    drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "CTmin",
       x = "Critical Thermal Minimum (°C)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
out.min #no outliers

#visualize CTmax outliers
out.max <- ggplot(df_flagged, aes(x = CTmax.C, fill = is_outlier_max)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "#d95f02"),
                    name = "Data Status",
                    labels = c("Normal", "Outlier"),
                    drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "CTmax",
       x = "Critical Thermal Maximum (°C)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
out.max #outliers for swordtail and mosquitofish

((out.min/out.max) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") + plot_layout(guides = "collect"))

#filter for rows where either CTmax OR CTmin is an outlier
outlier_individuals <- df_flagged %>%
  filter(is_outlier_max | is_outlier_min) %>%
  select(Species, Sex, Name, CTmax.C, CTmin.C, is_outlier_max, is_outlier_min)
outlier_individuals #all females except 1 male

#filter out outliers from df
O.rawTempData <- df_flagged %>%
  filter(!is_outlier_max & !is_outlier_min)
```

```{r}
#remove unnecessary columns
O.datTot <- O.rawTempData[,-c(4:6)]

    cols = c(CTmax.C, CTmin.C),

    values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(

      Trial,
      "CTmax.C" = "CTmax",
      "CTmin.C" = "CTmin"))

#gather summary stats
O.summ.stats <- O.dat.long %>%
  group_by(Species, Trial) %>%
  summarize(
    mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min  = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    med  = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max  = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

#get n for each sex in each species
O.sex.df <- O.datTot %>%
  count(Species, Sex) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0)

#final table
O.summ.stats.all <- O.summ.stats %>%
  left_join(O.sex.df, by = "Species") %>%
  mutate(
    mean_sd = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean, sd))

O.summ.stats.all
```

## Size stats

When separated by sex and species, we see that there appears to be an overlap between small swordtail males and swordtail females (although they differ from large swordtail males), overlap between males and females in sailfins, and very little overlap among males and females in mosquitofish. This is confirmed through wilcoxon/kruskal-wallis tests: sailfin males and females show no significant difference in length with a small effect size (although wide CI may indicate uncertainty in magnitude and direction of any small difference), male and female mosquitofish show a significant difference in size with a large effect size indicating females are almost always larger than males, and swordtail sex categories (female, large male, small male) show a significant difference in length (as expected since male classes are separated by size), with a significant pairwise comparison among all groups and a large effect size indicating small males < females < large males. 

Sexual dimorphism in length was evident for mosquitofish and among sex/morph groups in swordtails (although direction of size difference varied among morphs). Evidence for sexual dimorphism in our sailfin was inconclusive, with negligible effect sizes but a wide confidence interval.

Overall collinearity is low for CTmax and CTmin trials, but separation by species shows low collinearity of sex and size for sailfins in both trial types and high collinearity of sex and size for mosquitofish in both trial types (makes sense since males and females showed little overlap in size for mosquitofish). Collinearity is high for size and sex/morph class in swordtails, which again makes sense because male classes are determined by size. Will need to interpret model results with this in mind (can't really detect a sex-only difference after accounting for similar sizes in mosquitofish and swordtail because there are no similar sizes in swordtails).

**Length comparisons and effect size**

```{r}

#separate male classes in swordtails
O.size.data <- O.datTot %>%
  mutate(
    SizeGroup = case_when(
      Species == "Swordtail" & Sex == "female" ~ "Female",
      Species == "Swordtail" & Sex == "male" & Size.cat == "large" ~ "Large male",
      Species == "Swordtail" & Sex == "male" & Size.cat == "small" ~ "Small male",
      Species != "Swordtail" ~ as.character(Sex),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_))


#normality check by sex and species
O.normal <- O.size.data %>%
  group_by(Species, SizeGroup) %>%
summarize(statistic =shapiro.test(Size.mm)$statistic,
          p.value = shapiro.test(Size.mm)$p.value)

O.normal #all normal except female swordtail


#non-parametric test for size difference by species
O.size.test <- O.datTot %>%
  filter(Species != "Swordtail") %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarize(stat = wilcox.test(Size.mm ~ Sex)$statistic,
            p_value = wilcox.test(Size.mm~Sex)$p.value)

O.size.test #not significant for sailfin, but significant for mosquitofish

O.sw.size.test <- O.size.data %>%
  filter(Species == "Swordtail") %>%
  summarize(stat = kruskal.test(Size.mm ~ SizeGroup)$statistic,
            p_value = kruskal.test(Size.mm ~ SizeGroup)$p.value)

O.sw.size.test #significant difference among sex categories; makes sense since the male classes are determined by size

O.pw.dat <- O.size.data %>%
  filter(Species == "Swordtail")
O.pw.test <- pairwise.wilcox.test( O.pw.dat$Size.mm, O.pw.dat$SizeGroup, p.adjust.method = "holm")

O.pw.test #all pairs significantly different


#testing effect size
O.eff.size.tbl <- O.datTot %>%
  filter(Species != "Swordtail") %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise({
    cd <- effsize::cliff.delta(Size.mm ~ Sex)
    tibble(
      delta= cd$estimate,
    CI_low = cd$conf.int[1],
    CI_high = cd$conf.int[2])})

O.eff.size.tbl #sailfins with small effect size (-0.18) but wide CI (-0.51, 0.21) so there is uncertainty in the magnitude and direction of sexual size dimorphism. mosquitofish on the other hand show a large effect size with females being larger than males (0.98, CI 0.89, 0.997).

comparison <- list(
  c("Female", "Small male"),
  c("Female", "Large male"),
  c("Small male", "Large male"))

O.sw.eff.size <- bind_rows(lapply(comparison, function (g) {
  x <- O.pw.dat$Size.mm[O.pw.dat$SizeGroup == g[1]]
  y <- O.pw.dat$Size.mm[O.pw.dat$SizeGroup == g[2]]
  cd <- effsize::cliff.delta(x,y)
  
  tibble(
    group1 = g[1],
    group2 = g[2],
    delta = unname(cd$estimate),
    CI_low = cd$conf.int[1],
    CI_high = cd$conf.int[2])  }))

O.sw.eff.size #large size effects for all three combos; size ranking as follows: small males -> females -> large males


```

**Collinearity** 

```{r}
### CTmax ###
model1 <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)

vif(model1) #shows low levels of collinearity for all effects

vif.spp <- O.datTot %>%
  filter(Species != "Swordtail") %>% #since there are distinct size classes here
  group_by(Species) %>%
  group_modify( ~ {
    model <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = .x, REML = FALSE)
    v <- vif(model)
    
    tibble(
      Predictor = names(v),
      VIF = as.numeric(v), 
      Singular = isSingular(model)) }) %>%
  ungroup()

vif.spp #low collinearity for sailfins, but high for mosquitofish; makes sense since we saw large sexual size dimorphism in this species

vif.sw <- O.size.data %>%
  filter(Species == "Swordtail") %>% 
  group_modify( ~ {
    model <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ SizeGroup + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = .x, REML = FALSE)
    v <- vif(model)
    
    tibble::rownames_to_column(
      as.data.frame(v),
      var = "Predictor") %>%
      mutate(Singular = isSingular(model)) }) %>%
  ungroup()
vif.sw #adjusted GVIF for size group and size.mm indicate strong collinearity among size and sex/morph class; makese sense since the males are separated by size, but will need to keep this in mind when interpreting results. singular fit shows no variation in trial runs
```

# **Analysis**

## **CTmax**

### Model Selection

Here, we will run linear mixed effects models with CTmax as our dependent variable, and sex, species, and size (plus their interaction) as our independent variables. We will select our final model based on ΔAIC scores from the 'MuMln' package.

**Results:** The model containing just species as a dependent variable was the most supported in our model selection (ΔAICc=0.0; weight=0.511). Adding size (mod1b) or sex (mod1c) or both (mod1d) did not improve fit, but as they are characters of interest will will still examine the coefficients for comparison.

```{r}
# All models
mod1 <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #does CTmax differ among spp?
mod1b <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #is body size associated with CTmax after accounting for species?
mod1c <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + Sex + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #is sex associated with CTmax after accounting for species?
mod1d <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)       #are sex and size independently associated with CTmax? *Remember collinearity
mod1e <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species + Sex * Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)
      #does the relationship between size and CTmax differ between males and females?
mod1f <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species * Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)
      #do sex-associated differences in CTmax vary among species, after accounting for size?
mod1g <- lmer(CTmax.C ~ Species *Size.mm + Sex + (1|file.id.max), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #does body size and CTmax vary among species after accounting for sex?

# Model selection
model.sel(mod1, mod1b, mod1c, mod1d, mod1e, mod1f, mod1g)

  ### Mod1e (species+sex*size effects) is the most supported model (ΔAICc=0; weight=0.436)
  ### Species only (mod1) shows moderate support (ΔAICc=1.90; weight=0.168)
  ### Species interactive effects (mod1f&g) and size (mod1b) and sex (mod1c) alone showed very weak support

```

### Residual checks

Here, we will check if the model residuals are normal and homoscedastic using the 'DHARMa' package.

**Results:** All models showed no outlier deviation or heteroscedasticity. 

```{r}

# Species only model
simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(mod1, n = 1000)

plot(simulationOutput)

plotResiduals(simulationOutput)
plotResiduals(simulationOutput, form = O.rawTempData$Species)

  ### All good!


# Species and size * sex model
simulationOutput2 <- simulateResiduals(mod1e, n = 1000)

plot(simulationOutput2)

plotResiduals(simulationOutput2)
plotResiduals(simulationOutput2, form = O.rawTempData$Species)
plotResiduals(simulationOutput2, form = O.rawTempData$Size.mm)
plotResiduals(simulationOutput2, form = O.rawTempData$Sex)


  ### significant combined quatile deviation for upper quantile, only when plotted by size

# Species and sex model


```


### Model Summary

We will determine the overall effect of species (anova from 'lmerTest' package; using Satterthwaite approximation due to small sample size of random effect), and calculate the estimated marginal means and a pairwise species comparison (emmeans package). Model summaries will provide us with the effect of sex and size on the model. 

**Results:** There is a significant effect of species for CTmax (P<0.001). Pairwise comparisons show significant differences among swordtails-sailfin (p<0.001), swordtails-mosquitofish (p<0.001), but not sailfin-mosquitofish (p=0.174). The sex:size interaction was confirmed as a significant predictor in the model (p=0.010). However, lack of overlap between sizes in sexes in two of three species, single slope assumption among males and females within the model, and the lack of species-specific size slopes within the model makes biological interpretation of mod1e tenuous. 

```{r}
# SPECIES ONLY MODEL
 ## Overall species effect
anova(mod1, type = 2, ddf = "Satterthwaite") #significant (p<0.001)

 ## EMM & Pairwise comparisons

PW.sp.max <- emmeans(mod1, "Species", lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
summary(PW.sp.max) #EMM
summary(pairs(PW.sp.max), infer = c(TRUE,TRUE), level = 0.95, adjust = "holm") #Pairwise results
      
 ## Plotting EMM

PW.df <- as.data.frame(confint(PW.sp.max))

ggplot(PW.df, aes(x=Species, y=emmean)) +
  geom_point(size=2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lower.CL, ymax=upper.CL), width=0.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10)) +
  ylab("Predicted mean temperature (°C) \n") +
  xlab("\n Species") +
  theme_classic()

# SPECIES & SIZE MODEL

summary(mod1e)
anova(mod1e, type = 2, ddf = "Satterthwaite") #species significant (p<0.001), sex significant (p=0.006) and sex:size significant (p=0.010) but not size (p=0.34)

#mod1e assumes one common size-temp slope for males and for females, and no species-specific size slopes. however, we know from our size analysis that there are different size-sex relationships among our species

## this plot shows heterogeneity in the size-CTmax relationships among species; plus the male slope for swordtails is driven by the size morph classes
ggplot(model.frame(mod1e), aes(x=Size.mm, y=CTmax.C, color=Sex)) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y~x, se=TRUE) + 
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales="free_x") + 
  theme_classic()

slopes <- emtrends(mod1e, ~Sex, var = "Size.mm")
summary(slopes, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) #show a general negative trend for females (CTmax decreases with size) and general positive trend for males (CTmax increases with size) which isn't consistent with species-specific trends in graph above. also slopes are no significantly different than zero

pairs(slopes) #does show a significant difference between males and females, but again, this difference could be driven by species-specific differences in size-sex relationships

# SUMMARY TABLE
coef.table <- function(model, label, trait) {
  as.data.frame(coef(summary(model))) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Predictor") %>%
    filter(grepl(trait, Predictor)) %>%
    mutate(Model = label) %>%
    mutate(
      CI_low = Estimate - qt(0.975, df) * `Std. Error`,
      CI_high = Estimate + qt(0.975, df) * `Std. Error`) }

ctmax.results <- bind_rows(
  coef.table(mod1b, "B", "Size.mm"),
  coef.table(mod1c, "C", "^Sex"),
  coef.table(mod1d, "D", "Size.mm|^Sex"),
  coef.table(mod1e, "E", "Size.mm|^Sex"))
  
ctmax.results

```

### Sensitivity analysis

As our design has single-species runs, we test the sensitivity of our results to the variance estimated for clustered experimental trials. CR2 (cluster-robust standard errors) with Satterthwaite small-sample correction will be used.

**RESULTS:** Sex:size interaction remains significant using CR2. Overall species effect is still significant, and pairwise results reflect the conclusions from above analyses. 

```{r}
library(clubSandwich)
#robust coeff for mod1e
conf_int(mod1e, vcov = "CR2", level = 0.95, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE) #sex:size interaction still significant

#overall species effects

robVCV.spp.max <- vcovCR(mod1, type = "CR2")

Wald_test(mod1, constraints = constrain_zero(grep("^Species", names(fixef(mod1)))), vcov = robVCV.spp.max, test = "HTZ")

#pairwise analysis
PW.pairs.max <- pairs(PW.sp.max)
K <- as.matrix(PW.pairs.max@linfct)
rownames(K) <- as.character(summary(PW.pairs.max)$contrast)

rob.pairs.max <- linear_contrast(mod1, vcov = robVCV.spp.max, contrasts =K, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE, adjustment_method = "holm")

rob.pairs.max

```


## **CTmin**

### Model Selection

We will repeat the above analysis with CTmin as our dependent variable, and sex, species, and size (plus their interaction) as our independent variables. Then select our final model based on ΔAIC scores.

**Results:** The model containing species, sex, and size as dependent variables was the most supported in our model selection (ΔAICc=0.0; weight=0.267), but models containing just species + size (mod2b), species + sex (mod2c) or species only (mod2) had similar ΔAICc and weight values, meaning all 4 models are a competitive fit. 

```{r}
# All models
mod2 <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #does CTmin differ among spp?
mod2b <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species + Size.mm + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #is body size associated with CTmin after accounting for species?
mod2c <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species + Sex + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE) 
      #is sex associated with CTmin after accounting for species?
mod2d <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species + Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)       #are sex and size independently associated with CTmin? *Remember collinearity
mod2e <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species + Sex * Size.mm + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)
      #does the relationship between size and CTmin differ between males and females?
mod2f <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species * Sex + Size.mm + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)
      #do sex-associated differences in CTmin vary among species, after accounting for size?
mod2g <- lmer(CTmin.C ~ Species *Size.mm + Sex + (1|file.id.min), data = O.datTot, REML = FALSE)
      #does body size and CTmin vary among species after accounting for sex?

# Model selection
model.sel(mod2, mod2b, mod2c, mod2d, mod2e, mod2f, mod2g)

  ### Mod2d (species + sex + size) is the most supported model (ΔAICc=0; weight=0.323), although mod2b (species + size) and mod2c (species + sex) are also supported (mod2b: ΔAICc=0.18; weight=0.295; mod2c: ΔAICc=2.06; weight=0.115). Mod2e (species + sex*size) and Mod2 (species only) also shows moderate to weak support (Mod2e: ΔAICc=2.43; weight=0.096; mod2: ΔAICc=2.56; weight=0.090).
  ### Species interactive effects (mod1f&g) showed very weak support

```

### Sensitivity analysis

As our design has single-species runs, we test the sensitivity of our results to the variance estimated for clustered experimental trials. CR2 (cluster-robust standard errors) with Satterthwaite small-sample correction will be used.

**RESULTS:** Sex remains non-significant using CR2 in sex-only and combined model, but now size is also non-significant in individual model of species+size and combined model. The sex*size interaction is still not significant. Overall species effect is still significant, and pairwise results remain the same (although the p-value for the mosquitofish-sailfin contrast is no longer marginal, p=0.223).

```{r}

conf_int(mod2c, vcov = "CR2", level = 0.95, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE) #species still sig, but still not sex
conf_int(mod2d, vcov = "CR2", level = 0.95, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE) #neither sex nor size sig
conf_int(mod2e, vcov = "CR2", level = 0.95, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE) #interaction effect still not sig

#overall species effects

Wald_test(mod2, constraints = constrain_zero(grep("^Species", names(fixef(mod2)))), vcov = robVCV.spp.min, test = "HTZ")
```

## **Across male morphs**

Males in the Panuco swordtail have three morphs determined by copy number at mc4r locus: large males (SL >= 32mm), intermediate males (26 < SL < 36), and small males (SL <= 25mm with defined gonopodium). The morphs have greater variation in size than the variation between large males and females. We compare thermal tolerance across male morphs (only large and small, no intermediate in our study) and females. 

### Models

For both CTmax and CTmin, a model of temperature ~ sex category was the most supported, although adding size was also competative for CTmax. 

```{r}

### CTmin ###

model.sel(SWmod4, SWmod5, SWmod6)
```

# **Power Analysis**

Based on the power of our current study, we will calculate the average temperature difference needed to detect a significant sex effect. 

**Results:** The actual temperature difference between males and females in each category was much lower than the simulated temperature differences needed to detect a sex effect given the power of our study (Actual: CTmax=0.2, CTmin=0.1; Simulated: CTmax=0.6, CTmin=0.3). While we found no statistically significant sex effect in any temperature category, smaller biologically meaningful differences can not be ruled out due to our limited sample size.

***NOTE:*** This will increase loading time; to reduce loading time, remove/comment out the following section and keep the comparisons table to view results.

Power simulation:

```{r}
# Function to simulate power and estimate minimum detectable sex difference
# Inputs:
#   data: dataset containing Temp, Species, Sex, and Trial ID columns
#   nsim: number of simulations per effect size (default = 1000)
#   delta_range: vector of sex differences in °C to test (default = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.1))
#   alpha: significance threshold (default = 0.05)   
#   power_target: desired power (default = 0.80)
#   seed: random seed for reproducibility (default = 123)
# Automatically extracted from data:
#   nM, nF: number of males and females within each species
#   sigma_resid: residual standard deviation from the mixed model
#   sigma_trial: trial-level random-intercept standard deviation
#   Species: species identities
#   Trial: experimental trial IDs
# Statistical model:
#   Temp ~ Species + Sex + (1|Trial)
# Significance assessed using Type II ANOVA w/ Satterthwiate-approximated ddf
# Outputs:
#   power_curve: estimate power across simulate sex differences
#   MMD: minimum tested sex difference achieving target power
#   residual_SD: estimated residual standard deviation
#   trial_SD: estimated trial-level standard deviation



simulate_MDD_mixed <- function(data, nsim = 1000,
                               delta_range = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.1),
                               alpha = 0.05,
                               power_target = 0.8,
                               seed = 123) {

  set.seed(seed)

  # Expected columns: Temp, Species, Sex, Trial
  df <- data[complete.cases(
    data[, c("Temp", "Species", "Sex", "Trial")]), ]

  df$Species <- factor(df$Species)
  df$Trial <- factor(df$Trial)

  # Accept either F/M or Female/Male labels
  df$Sex <- as.character(df$Sex)
  df$Sex[df$Sex == "F"] <- "female"
  df$Sex[df$Sex == "M"] <- "male"
  df$Sex <- factor(df$Sex, levels = c("female", "male"))

  if (anyNA(df$Sex)) {
    stop("Check Sex labels: expected female/male or F/M.") }

  # Estimate variance components from observed data
  base <- lmerTest::lmer(
    Temp ~ Species + Sex + (1 | Trial),
    data = df,
    REML = TRUE)

  sigma_resid <- sigma(base)

  sigma_trial <- as.numeric(
    attr(VarCorr(base)$Trial, "stddev"))[1]

  # Retain fitted species means but set the true sex
  # difference to zero before adding simulated effects
  beta <- fixef(base)
  beta[grepl("^Sex", names(beta))] <- 0

  X <- model.matrix(~ Species + Sex, data = df)
  mu <- as.numeric(
    X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE] %*% beta)

  results <- lapply(delta_range, function(delta) {

    pvals <- replicate(nsim, {

      # Simulate one random intercept per trial
      trial_effect <- rnorm(
        nlevels(df$Trial),
        mean = 0,
        sd = sigma_trial)

      sim_df <- df

      sim_df$Temp <- mu +
        delta * (df$Sex == "male") +
        trial_effect[as.integer(df$Trial)] +
        rnorm(nrow(df), 0, sigma_resid)

      # Fit same mixed model as the primary analysis
      fit <- tryCatch(
        suppressMessages(
        suppressWarnings(
          lmerTest::lmer(
            Temp ~ Species + Sex + (1 | Trial),
            data = sim_df,
            REML = FALSE))),
        error = function(e) NULL)

      if (is.null(fit)) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        tryCatch(
          as.numeric(
            anova(
              fit,
              type = 2,
              ddf = "Satterthwaite"
           )["Sex", "Pr(>F)"]),
          error = function(e) NA_real_)}
    })

    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(pvals))

    data.frame(
      delta = delta,
      power = if (n_valid > 0) {
        mean(pvals < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
      } else NA_real_,
      valid = n_valid)
  })

  power_results <- bind_rows(results)

  # First detectable difference reaching target power
  idx <- which(power_results$power >= power_target)[1]

  mdd <- if (is.na(idx)) NA_real_ else {
    power_results$delta[idx] }

  list(
    power_curve = power_results,
    MDD = mdd,
    residual_SD = sigma_resid,
    trial_SD = sigma_trial) 
}
######### END FUNCTION ##########

# CTmax
dat_max <- data.frame(
  Temp = O.datTot$CTmax.C,
  Species = O.datTot$Species,
  Sex = O.datTot$Sex,
  Trial = O.datTot$file.id.max)

# CTmin
dat_min <- data.frame(
  Temp = O.datTot$CTmin.C,
  Species = O.datTot$Species,
  Sex = O.datTot$Sex,
  Trial = O.datTot$file.id.min)

MDD_CTmax <- simulate_MDD_mixed(dat_max)
MDD_CTmin <- simulate_MDD_mixed(dat_min)

MDD_CTmax$MDD
MDD_CTmin$MDD

power_all <- bind_rows(
  mutate(MDD_CTmax$power_curve,
         Trait = "CTmax", MDD = MDD_CTmax$MDD),
  mutate(MDD_CTmin$power_curve,
         Trait = "CTmin", MDD = MDD_CTmin$MDD))

ggplot(power_all, aes(delta, power, color = Trait)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = MDD),
             linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(
    x = "Sex difference (°C)",
    y = "Estimated power",
    color = "Trait") +
  theme_classic() + 
  scale_color_manual(name="Trait",
                    values = c("CTmax"="#E1AF00", "CTmin"="#78B7C5"),
                    labels = c("CTmax"="CTmax", "CTmin"="CTmin"))

```

# **Summary**

We were interested in whether the sexual dimorphism found in many livebearing species played a role in thermal tolerance. We tested for sex-biased tolerance in CTmax and CTmin trials in three livebearing species: sailfin mollies (*P. latipinna*), Western mosquitofish (*G. affinis*), and Panuco swordtail (*X. nigrensis*). We also tested whether male morphs (i.e. large and small males) within one species (swordtail) affected thermal tolerance.

In both trials (CTmax, CTmin), sex and size did ***not*** influence thermal tolerance. Instead, only species differences affected thermal tolerance. In general, mosquitofish tolerated the most extreme temperatures, followed by sailfin. Swordtails had the narrowest and weakest thermal tolerance, owing likely to the consistency of temperature at their place of origin (e.g spring-fed rivers).

Likewise, male morphs did ***not*** influence thermal tolerance, further confirming that this is likely no detectable sex-biased thermal differences in our current setup. 

A power analysis shows that the actual detected sex differences in both categories is much lower than the simulated temperature differences needed in order to detect a sex-based effect given the power of our study. Therefore, smaller biologically meaningful differences can not be ruled out due to our limited sample size.

```{r}
cr2.table <- function(model, trait, label) {
  V <- vcovCR(model, type = "CR2")
  
  as.data.frame(
    conf_int(model, vcov = V, level = 0.95, test = "Satterthwaite", p_values = TRUE)) %>%
    filter(Coef %in% c("Sexmale", "Size.mm")) %>%
    transmute(
      Trait = trait,
      Model = label,
      Predictor = Coef,
      CR2_Estimate = beta,
      CR2_SE = SE,
      CR2_low = CI_L,
      CR2_high = CI_U,
      CR2_p = p_val)
}

O.cr2.results <- bind_rows(
  cr2.table(mod2b, "CTmin", "B"),
  cr2.table(mod2c, "CTmin", "C"),
  cr2.table(mod2d, "CTmin", "D"),
  cr2.table(mod2e, "CTmin", "E"),
  cr2.table(mod1b, "CTmax", "B"),
  cr2.table(mod1c, "CTmax", "C"),
  cr2.table(mod1d, "CTmax", "D"),
  cr2.table(mod1e, "CTmax", "E"))

O.model.results <- bind_rows(
  ctmin.results %>% mutate(Trait = "CTmin"),
  ctmax.results %>% mutate(Trait = "CTmax")) %>%
  transmute(
    Trait,
    Model,
    Predictor,
    MB_Estimate = Estimate,
    MB_SE = `Std. Error`,
    MB_low = CI_low,
    MB_high = CI_high,
    MB_df = df,
    MB_p = `Pr(>|t|)`)

O.combined.results <- O.model.results %>%
  left_join(O.cr2.results, by = c("Trait", "Model", "Predictor")) %>%
  mutate(
    Trait = factor(Trait, levels = c("CTmin", "CTmax")),
    Model = factor(Model, levels = c("B", "C", "D", "E")), 
    Effect = case_when(
      Predictor == "Sexmale" ~ "Sex",
      Predictor == "Size.mm" ~ "Size", 
      TRUE ~ Predictor)) %>%
  arrange(Trait, Model, match(Predictor, c("Sexmale", "Size.mm")))

O.combined.results <- O.combined.results %>%
  mutate(
    p.disp.mb = case_when(
      MB_p < 0.001 ~ "*p* < 0.001",
      MB_p < 0.05  ~ paste0(sprintf("%.3f", MB_p)),
      TRUE            ~ sprintf("%.3f", MB_p))) %>%
  mutate(
    p.disp.cr2 = case_when(
      CR2_p < 0.001 ~ "*p* < 0.001",
      CR2_p < 0.05  ~ paste0(sprintf("%.3f", CR2_p)),
      TRUE            ~ sprintf("%.3f", CR2_p)))

O.table.results <- O.combined.results %>%
  mutate(
    Model = dplyr::recode(
      as.character(Model),
      "B" = "Species + Size",
      "C" = "Species + Sex",
      "D" = "Species + Sex \n+Size",
      "E" = "Species + Sex*Size")) %>%
  transmute(
    Trait,
    Model,
    Effect,
    mb_est = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", MB_Estimate, MB_SE),
    mb_ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", MB_low, MB_high),
    mb_df = sprintf("%.2f", MB_df),
    mb_p = p.disp.mb,
    
    cr2_est = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", CR2_Estimate, CR2_SE),
    cr2_ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", CR2_low, CR2_high),
    cr2_p = p.disp.cr2)

O.coeff.table <- O.table.results %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "Model", groupname_col = "Trait", row_group_as_column = TRUE) %>%
  tab_stubhead(label = "Model") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Model-based inference", columns = c(Effect, mb_est, mb_ci, mb_df, mb_p)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "CR2 analysis", columns = c(cr2_est, cr2_ci, cr2_p)) %>%
  cols_label(
    Effect = "Effect",
    mb_est = "Estimate (SE)",
    mb_ci = "95% CI", 
    mb_df = "df",
    mb_p = md("*p*-value"), 
    cr2_est = "Estimate (SE)",
    cr2_ci = "95% CI",
    cr2_p = md("*p*-value")) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "right", color = "lightgray", weight = px(1.5)),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(Effect,mb_est, mb_ci,mb_df, cr2_est, cr2_ci))) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "right", color = "lightgray", weight = px(2)),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(mb_p))) %>%
  cols_align("center", everything()) %>%
  opt_horizontal_padding(scale = 2)

O.coeff.table

gtsave(O.coeff.table, "OnlineResource4_coefficients.rtf")
```

### Sex & size

```{r}

#install.packages("lme4")

### CTmax- sex and size

# Extract observations used in the full model
df.max <- model.frame(mod1d)

# Generate predictions only within each observed species x sex size range
pred.max <- df.max %>%
  group_by(Species, Sex) %>%
  reframe(
    Size.mm = seq(
      min(Size.mm),
      max(Size.mm),
      length.out = 50))

# Construct fixed-effect design matrix
X <- model.matrix(
  delete.response(
    terms(lme4::nobars(formula(mod1d)))),
  data = pred.max)

# Model coefficients and covariance matrix
beta <- lme4::fixef(mod1d)
V <- as.matrix(vcov(mod1d))

X <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]
V <- V[names(beta), names(beta), drop = FALSE]

# Predicted means and approximate 95% confidence intervals
pred.max$fit <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)

pred.max$SE <- sqrt(
  rowSums((X %*% V) * X))

pred.max$lower <- pred.max$fit - 1.96 * pred.max$SE
pred.max$upper <- pred.max$fit + 1.96 * pred.max$SE

# Plot
O.sex.size.plot.max <- ggplot(df.max, aes(x = Size.mm, y = CTmax.C, color = Sex)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape= Sex), alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred.max, aes(
      x = Size.mm,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      fill = Sex,
      group = Sex),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(
    data = pred.max, aes(x = Size.mm, y = fit, color = Sex, group = Sex),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n=5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Body size (mm)",
    y = "CTmax (°C)",
    color = "Sex",
    fill = "Sex") +

                     values = c("female" = 16, "male" = 17),
                     labels = c("female"="Female", "male"="Male")) +
  scale_color_manual(name="Sex",
                     values = c("female"="#E1AF00", "male"="#78B7C5"),
                     labels = c("female"="Female", "male"="Male")) +
  scale_fill_manual(name="Sex",
                     values = c("female"="#E1AF00", "male"="#78B7C5"),
                     labels = c("female"="Female", "male"="Male")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"), 
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"),

O.sex.size.plot.max



### CTmin- sex and size
# Extract observations used in the full model
df.min <- model.frame(mod2d)

# Generate predictions only within each observed species x sex size range
pred.min <- df.min %>%
  group_by(Species, Sex) %>%
  reframe(
    Size.mm = seq(
      min(Size.mm),
      max(Size.mm),
      length.out = 50))

# Construct fixed-effect design matrix
X2 <- model.matrix(
  delete.response(

V2 <- V2[names(beta2), names(beta2), drop = FALSE]

pred.min$SE <- sqrt(
  rowSums((X2 %*% V2) * X2))

pred.min$lower <- pred.min$fit - 1.96 * pred.min$SE
pred.min$upper <- pred.min$fit + 1.96 * pred.min$SE

# Plot
```

### Model diagnostics

```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### CTmax & CTmin model selection ###
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
max.sel <- model.sel(mod1, mod1b, mod1c, mod1d, mod1e, mod1f, mod1g)
min.sel <- model.sel(mod2, mod2b, mod2c, mod2d, mod2e, mod2f, mod2g)

prepare.sel <- function(sel, trait) {
  as.data.frame(sel) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
    mutate(Trait = trait) %>%
    select(Trait, Model, df, AICc, delta, weight)}

sel.all <- bind_rows(
  prepare.sel(min.sel, "CTmin"),
  prepare.sel(max.sel, "CTmax")) %>%
  mutate(Trait = factor(Trait, levels = c("CTmin", "CTmax"))) %>%
  mutate(Model = dplyr::recode(
    as.character(Model),
    mod1 = "Species",
    mod1b = "Species + Size",
    mod1c = "Species + Sex",
    mod1d = "Species + Size \n+Sex",
    mod1e = "Species + \nSize * Sex",
    mod1f = "Species * Sex \n+ Size",
    mod1g = "Species * Size \n+ Sex",
    mod2 = "Species",
    mod2b = "Species + Size",
    mod2c = "Species + Sex",
    mod2d = "Species + Size \n+Sex",
    mod2e = "Species + \nSize * Sex",
    mod2f = "Species * Sex \n+ Size",
    mod2g = "Species * Size \n+ Sex"))

O.model.table <- sel.all %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "Model", groupname_col = "Trait", row_group_as_column = TRUE) %>%
  #tab_stubhead(label = "Model") %>%
  cols_label(
    Model = "Model",
    df = "df",
    AICc = "AICc",
    delta = "ΔAICc",
    weight = "Weight") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(AICc, delta), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = weight, decimals = 3) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "right", color = "lightgray", weight = px(1.5)),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(df, AICc, delta)))

O.model.table

gtsave(O.model.table, "OnlineResource4_model-sel.rtf")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### CTmax & CTmin main model diagnostics ###
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(DHARMa)

# Simulate residuals once
sim.max <- simulateResiduals(mod1, n = 1000)
sim.min <- simulateResiduals(mod2, n = 1000)

build_diagnostic_plot <- function() {
  
  oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(oldpar))
  
  # Three rows, two columns
  par(
    mfrow = c(3, 2),
    mar = c(4, 4, 3.5, 1),
    cex = 0.75,
    family = "sans")
  
  # A: CTmax QQ
  plotQQunif(
    sim.max,
    main = "A. CTmax: species-only model checks")
  
  # B: CTmin QQ
  plotQQunif(
    sim.min,
    main = "B. CTmin: species-only model checks")
  
  # C: CTmax residuals vs predicted
  plotResiduals(sim.max)
  
  # D: CTmin residuals vs predicted
  plotResiduals(sim.min)
  
  # E: CTmax residuals vs species
  plotResiduals(sim.max, form = as.factor(model.frame(mod1)$Species))
  
  # F: CTmin residuals vs species
  plotResiduals(sim.min, form = as.factor(model.frame(mod2)$Species))
}

# TIFF
tiff(
  "OnlineResource4_mainResidChecks.tiff",
  width = 6.85,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",
  res = 600,
  compression = "lzw",
  type = "cairo")
build_diagnostic_plot()
dev.off()

# EPS

cairo_ps(
  "OnlineResource4_mainResidChecks.eps",
  width = 6.85,
  height = 7,
  onefile = FALSE,
  fallback_resolution = 600)
build_diagnostic_plot()
dev.off()
```
